alignments.note: 1cs suffix on נֶפֶשׁ realized by the possessive *My* (rule 18).

The clause נַפְשִׁי לַאדֹנָי is verbless; *waiteth* is a supplied lexical verb, not the construction-supplied copula, since it predicates an event of waiting the Hebrew never writes, so it is `added` under rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause. The ASV italic corroborates and decides nothing (rule 7). The competing reading would attach it to the לְ under rule 49, but that rule places a copula, and *waiteth for* is not one.
אֲדֹנָ takes *the Lord*, the supplied *the* joining the noun under rule 15 (rule 57).
The 1cs suffix of the title אֲדֹנָי is lexicalized in the name and the ASV writes no possessive anywhere in it (rule 57).

Comparative מִן rendered *More than*, headed on *than*, the degree adverb being what English adds to a comparison it writes elsewhere without one (rule 24). The second *more than*, standing over the third colon which writes no מִן of its own, is the same morpheme's distributed scope and joins its one discontinuous unit under rule 25 rather than being `added`; the ASV italic on it corroborates the supply and decides nothing (rule 7).
Anarthrous substantival participle שֹׁמְרִים → *watchmen* (rule 46), headed on the word carrying the lexeme.

*wait* is the supplied predicate of the elided comparative clause; the Hebrew writes no verb for it, and the participle's own lexeme is already written in *watchmen*, which rule 31's subtraction leaves whole when *wait* is dropped, so it is `added` under rule 34's boundary. The competing reading takes *watchmen wait* as one rendering of s007; that was set aside because the participle is rendered as a noun and *wait* answers to the gapped predicate of the parallel line, which the Hebrew never writes.
Article assimilated into the pointed preposition, still a real token, aligned to the written *the* (rules 12, 15).

No conjunction morpheme stands in the third colon, so the connective *Yea* answers to no morpheme and is its own `added` unit under rule 14's closing sentences; it is not folded into the participle or the comparative beside it, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and*.
Second anarthrous substantival participle → *watchmen* (rule 46). This is a fresh occurrence the ASV renders, not a repetition to be marked `unrepresented` under rule 22.
Assimilated article aligned to the written *the* (rules 12, 15).

review_notes: Three ASV italics in the verse are read separately: *waiteth* and *wait* are supplied lexical verbs answering to no morpheme and are `added`, while the italic *more than* of the third colon is the written מִן's distributed scope under rule 25 and is not `added`. Rule 7 governs — the markup is evidence, not a label.
The whole verse is one comparative construction with the two watchmen cola juxtaposed asyndetically; the supplied *Yea* is the only connective in the English and no waw stands for it.
